items.title: Why Do the Houses Pray?
items.task: Look at the roof. What shape is it making?
items.reveal: Gassho-zukuri: like hands in prayer. Steep, to shed snow.

question.text: Which roof sheds a heavy snow load better?

choices.response: Snow sits. Think of a slide.

items.title: No Nails?
items.task: If a house is open, look at joints. Rope, wood, pegs.
items.reveal: Some frames use joinery and rope more than big iron nails. Check the exact wording before live.
items.notes: Confirm joinery / ‘no nails’ wording. Later repairs may use metal.

items.title: What's Upstairs?
items.task: The attic was not only storage.
items.reveal: Silkworms. A house that was also a workshop.
items.notes: Confirm attic sericulture in gassho houses before live.

items.title: Village From Above
items.task: From a viewpoint, tick three survival pieces: river, fields, forest, roofs, paths.

items.title: House or Factory?
items.task: Sleeping, cooking, silk, snow. Is this a home, a factory, or both?

items.title: Four Metres of Snow
items.weirdFact: Winters here can bury a house. Check typical depths before we print four metres as a fact.
items.notes: Confirm regional snowfall figures. Do not treat four metres as every winter.
